hook: A blowtorch on the front. His bare hand on the back.
narration: A blowtorch on the front of this block. His bare hand on the back.
It is a piece of the heat shield for NASA's Parker Solar Probe, built to fly closer to the Sun than anything before it.
Inside is carbon foam between thin carbon sheets. It is very light.
The real shield gets up to about twenty five hundred degrees Fahrenheit. This torch takes it to a couple hundred.
Thirty seconds in, the front starts to glow. [short pause]
outcome: And the back stayed cool to the touch.

location_card.place: Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Lab, Maryland

title: Blowtorch vs a Sun probe's heat shield
description:
In 2018, engineers on NASA's Parker Solar Probe showed how its heat shield works: a blowtorch heats the front of a sample panel while the back stays cool enough to touch.
